title: C24102890089
paper_title: 数据驱动下磁性元件的磁芯损耗建模

strengths: recognizes waveform geometry can be compressed into time/shape/frequency descriptors
uses confusion-matrix/classification metrics rather than accuracy alone in the paper narrative
risks: printed feature extractor is hard-coded to material1 rather than the full four-material training set
paper claims peak/kurtosis/skew/slope/frequency features while printed classifiers use an undefined X and inference selects mean/peak/std, so train/inference feature contract is not reproducible
printed RF uses 100 trees while prose says 500 and contains an unrelated copied sentence about selecting top-20 molecular descriptors
no printed implementation of the claimed MLP-RF probability-weighted ensemble
paper validation narrative and printed train_test_split path do not clearly describe the same evaluation sample source

strengths: keeps a named physics model as the baseline
compares residual behavior and MAPE/R2 across several temperature corrections
recognizes nonlinear parameter instability as a model-selection concern
risks: all reported model-comparison metrics are in-sample fit evidence; no held-out-temperature validation is shown

polynomial table is described as unstable although the two displayed initializations give nearly identical estimates except transcription/rounding, so the stated reason is not fully supported by the displayed table
scientific-notation/parameter transcription drifts appear between equations and parameter tables
temperature-saturation formula signs/parameter signs are inconsistent between prose/equations and printed code
Bm is taken as row-wise maximum without an explicit max-absolute or half-peak-to-peak convention check

strengths: maps the requested main effects and two-way interactions to explicit statistical terms
reports F and p values and provides interaction-model code rather than only descriptive means
risks: raw-loss ANOVA does not adjust for frequency and Bm, two strong continuous covariates, so factor and interaction effects can be confounded by operating-condition distributions
p values are treated as impact magnitude although statistical significance is not effect size
Table 19 is labeled waveform-material but its interaction row is labeled temperature-material and numerically repeats the temperature-waveform interaction, indicating likely copy/transcription drift
temperature-material interaction has p≈0.732, so any blanket claim that all factor pairs have significant synergy is unsupported
the minimum condition is selected by raw group-average loss without conditioning on frequency/Bm support

strengths: retains an interpretable physics baseline across waveform types
explicitly separates material/waveform regimes instead of forcing one opaque global parameter set
risks: generalization is claimed from fitting metrics without an independent grouped/out-of-condition test
Table 27/28 contain parameter transcription mismatches, including material2 sine alpha 1.7181 vs 1.781 and trapezoid coefficients changing across the two tables
printed Q4 code fits one selected file/sheet rather than showing the full 12-model routing pipeline
a 12-piece model needs an applicability-domain and routing contract; boundary behavior and sparse-regime support are not evaluated

strengths: keeps both loss and transmitted-energy proxy in the paper-level objective definition
recognizes material and waveform as discrete decision variables in the mathematical formulation
risks: printed code is scipy.optimize.minimize, not PSO, and omits waveform/material discrete variables, so it does not implement the claimed mixed-integer 12-model search
printed power-loss exponent f**2.7181 conflicts with the nearby material2 sine parameter alpha≈1.7181
paper-reported frequencies 694891/813076 exceed the printed f_max=320000 and the linear-result temperature 22 is below printed U_min=25
paper text gives PSO temperature 90 while Table 33 gives 70
exact smoke of the printed code converges to the boundary [f≈50000,Bm≈0.1,U≈90], not the reported point
ratio scalarization P/Q imposes a fixed preference and can hide the Pareto tradeoff; no Pareto front/support-domain check is shown

verified_text_evidence.claim: Q1 prose describes RF/MLP/weighted ensemble and evaluation; appendix later shows only separate RF/MLP classifiers
Q1 printed feature/classifier code has material1-only extraction, undefined X, and mean/peak/std inference features
Q2 model metrics/parameter-stability rationale and table values
Q3 interaction tables and actual statsmodels formulas
Q4 parameter tables contain cross-table coefficient drifts
Q5 paper claims PSO/mixed variables while printed code uses scipy minimize with narrower continuous bounds

transfer_lessons: Freeze a feature schema: raw extraction, training matrix, inference matrix and paper feature list must be machine-checked for identical names/order/transformations.
For factor-effect questions, adjust strong continuous covariates before interpreting categorical main effects/interactions; report effect sizes and uncertainty, not p values alone.
Use a parameter registry so equations, tables, code and optimization all read the same fitted coefficients; reject manual coefficient re-entry.
Every reported optimum must be re-evaluated by the exact objective and checked against every bound/category/support constraint before paper export.
A claimed algorithm name (PSO/GA/NSGA-II/etc.) must map to executable code of that algorithm; a generic local optimizer is not equivalent.
Generalization requires held-out conditions/groups; in-sample R2/MAPE is calibration evidence only.
